tools.name: search_flours
tools.description: Search the Pandough flour database. Returns flour names, protein %, W strength, hydration ranges, and types. Use this to help users find the right flour for their bake.

tools.name: get_flour_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific flour by its slug. Returns full profile including protein, W strength, hydration curve, maturation profiles, and description.

tools.name: list_recipes
tools.description: List the dough recipe styles plan_bake supports. Call this when a user names a style (Neapolitan, classica, focaccia, bread, baguette) so you pass the correct recipeSlug instead of guessing — and so you never confuse a style word like 'classica' with a flour whose name contains it.

tools.name: plan_bake
tools.description: Create a bake plan with ingredient calculations. Returns exact ingredient amounts in grams, an auto-sized yeast amount, a fermentation schedule, dough warnings, and a calculator URL the user can open in Pandough with all parameters prefilled. Before calling this, gather the inputs that actually determine a good plan (skip any the user already volunteered): (1) Strongly ask which oven model they use — call search_ovens and pass ovenSlug. If it is unlisted, ask for ovenType plus ovenMaxCelsius. Oven capability materially changes the hydration band and bake feasibility; if the user declines, proceed but say the result is not oven-adapted. (2) Which flour(s) do they have? — call search_flours to resolve a flourSlug (or pass flourBlend for a 2–5 flour cut, e.g. a Pulcinella base with 30% Manitoba); this is what makes hydration and warnings flour-aware. (3) Their room temperature and fridge temperature — pass roomTempCelsius/fridgeTempCelsius; temperature is the dominant driver of yeast amount and timing. (4) How they mix/knead (by hand, stand mixer, no-knead) — plan_bake does not return technique guidance, so pair it with a troubleshoot call for method advice. (5) Do they want a preferment? — pass `preferment` for a biga, poolish, tiga, cold/long biga, or a natural sourdough starter. The yeast figure accounts for the preferment, and the calculator link opens with the build already set up, so recommending a biga in prose without passing this param hands the user a direct dough. Don't interrogate a user who already gave a full brief.

recipeSlug.description: Recipe type slug. Supported: neapolitan-pizza, classica-pizza, focaccia, artisan-bread, baguette (call list_recipes for the full list). When the user names a style like 'classica', pass that style here — do NOT confuse it with a flour whose name happens to contain the word.

flourSlug.description: Flour slug from search_flours (e.g. 'caputo-pizzeria'). For a single flour. Mutually exclusive with flourBlend.

flourBlend.description: A weighted flour blend (2–5 flours summing to 100%), e.g. [{flourSlug:'caputo-pizzeria',percent:70},{flourSlug:'manitoba-oro',percent:30}]. Mutually exclusive with flourSlug.

percent.description: This flour's share of the blend (1–99); the set must sum to 100

roomTempHours.description: Room-temperature fermentation hours (0–168). Pass BOTH this and fridgeTempHours to lock the split; naming only a total lets the engine choose. These hours are the bulk before the fridge: when the fridge leg is above 0 the plan adds the recipe's final proof at room temperature after the fridge (a warm-up) on top of them, and says so. Room legs above 14h are clamped with a warning.

fridgeTempHours.description: Cold fermentation hours (0–168). Pass BOTH this and roomTempHours to lock the split. A locked fridge leg above 0 is followed by a warm-up at room temperature (the recipe's final proof), shown as its own schedule line.

stages.description: The full main-dough fermentation schedule as ordered stages (1–6), e.g. [{durationHours:1,tempCelsius:22},{durationHours:21,tempCelsius:4},{durationHours:2,tempCelsius:22}] for 1h at room temperature, 21h in the fridge, then a 2h warm-up. Use it when the user describes more than a room leg and a fridge leg, an order other than room then fridge, or a stage at its own temperature. The stages are the whole schedule: nothing is added (include the warm-up after the fridge yourself) and the calculator link opens on exactly these stages. Mutually exclusive with roomTempHours / fridgeTempHours. Room-temperature stages above 14h are clamped with a warning.

durationHours.description: Length of this stage in hours

tempCelsius.description: Temperature of this stage in °C (the fridge temperature for a cold stage)

roomTempCelsius.description: The user's real kitchen temperature in °C (2–40). The single biggest driver of yeast amount and timing — ask the user for it.

fridgeTempCelsius.description: The user's real fridge temperature in °C (0–12). Ask the user for it when a cold ferment is involved.

ovenSlug.description: Exact oven model slug from search_ovens. Strongly preferred: the engine uses the model's real ceiling and oven class to adapt hydration and bake feasibility. Mutually exclusive with manual ovenType/ovenMaxCelsius.

ovenType.description: Oven class for an unlisted model. Pass together with ovenMaxCelsius; prefer ovenSlug when search_ovens finds the model.

ovenMaxCelsius.description: The real maximum temperature in °C for an unlisted oven (100–600). This is what constrains hydration and bake time.

ovenMinCelsius.description: Optional minimum set temperature in °C for an unlisted oven.

bakeTime.description: Target bake time as an ISO 8601 datetime with the user's UTC offset for that date, e.g. '2026-06-10T18:00:00+02:00' for 18:00 in Warsaw in June (+01:00 in winter: the offset follows daylight saving time). 'Z' means UTC, not the user's local time. Must be in the future.

preferment.description: Plan the bake around a preferment (biga, poolish, tiga, sourdough…). The yeast figure returned accounts for it, and the calculator link opens with the build already set up.

type.description: Preferment style. poolish = 100% hydration, fast, extensible. biga = stiff (~45-50%). biga-fredda = one long cold hold. biga-lunga = 24h cold then 24h warm. tiga = tiga-style build. sourdough = natural starter (no commercial yeast).

percentFlour.description: Share of the TOTAL flour that goes into the preferment (1-100). Defaults: 30 for biga/poolish/tiga, 15 for sourdough.

hydrationPercent.description: Preferment hydration % (40-200). Defaults to the style's canonical value (poolish 100, biga ~45).

stages.description: The build program, leg by leg — e.g. [{durationHours:24,tempCelsius:4},{durationHours:24,tempCelsius:18}] for a long biga. Omit to use the style's default program.

durationHours.description: Length of this leg in hours

tempCelsius.description: Temperature of this leg in °C (use ~4 for the fridge)

flourSlug.description: Build the preferment from a specific flour (slug from search_flours). Omit to use the main flour.

locale.description: UI locale for the returned calculator link (e.g. 'en', 'pl', 'it'). Defaults to 'en'.

tools.name: troubleshoot
tools.description: Search the Pandough baking knowledge base for troubleshooting advice, technique guides, and flour science. Returns curated expert content about common baking issues.

issue.description: The baking issue or question (e.g. 'sticky dough', 'no oven spring', 'cold proof technique')

tools.name: search_ovens
tools.description: Search the Pandough oven database. Returns oven specs (max temperature, type, fuel) plus recommended bake settings — top/deck heat, bake time, and deck material — computed for a Neapolitan pizza by the same heat engine the site uses.

tools.name: list_active_bakes
tools.description: List the signed-in baker's scheduled and active bakes plus live temperature-sensor readings when a device is reporting. The first call prompts the chat app to authorize a Pandough account (OAuth scope bakes:read). Needs Pro (or cancelled-Pro). Returns ids, flour, hydration, schedule, a calculator session link, and probe temps (air around the dough, not dough core).
